text: I am the LORD your God, you shall have no other gods besides me.
You shall not make for yourself any carved image, or any likeness of anything; you shall not bow down to them nor serve them.
You shall not take the name of the LORD your God in vain.
Observe the Sabbath day, to keep it holy.
Honor your father and your mother.
You shall not murder.
You shall not commit adultery.
You shall not steal.
You shall not bear false witness.
You shall not covet anything that is your neighbor's.
Access to God is by Christ.
No man comes to the Father but by Christ.
Access to God needed to obtain mercy and grace.
Draw near to God and He will draw near to you.
Access to God is privileged to the saints of God.
If you seek God, He will be found by you; but if you forsake Him, He will cast you off.
The LORD is near to all who call upon Him in truth.
We are to earnestly seek God.
The wicked are commanded to seek God.
We are to urge others to seek God.
Those who are far from God shall perish, it is thus good to draw near to God.
Seek the LORD and you shall live.
All are required to have faith in God.
Christians required to believe in Christ and on His name.
Believe in Christ to do the work of God.
Faith needed to open relationship with God.
He that is faithful in that which is least is faithful also in much.
We are to believe in the gospel and scriptures.
We are to believe in what Moses and the prophets wrote.
Faith comes by hearing, and hearing by the word of God.
Whoever believes in Christ shall not be condemned, but have eternal life.
We are to put our trust in God as our help and shield (for he who trusts in the LORD, mercy shall surround him).
Blessed is the man who trusts in the LORD, and whose hope is in the LORD.
Watch, stand fast in the faith, be brave, be strong.
Do not put your faith and trust in materialistic wealth and security, but in the living God.
Your faith should not be in the wisdom of men butlin the power of God.
He that believes in Christ, believes in God the Father.
Those who believe in God should also be careful to maintain good works.
Trust in the LORD with all your heart, and lean not on your own understanding.
Blessed are they that have not seen Christ, and yet have believed.
Warnings against coming into unbelief.
Those who are guilty of unbelief have not the word of God in them and are not Christ's sheep.
Doubtfulness in the ways and power of God is forbidden.
The power to do great things is given to those that have faith and doubt not.
We are not to believe every spirit but try them whether they are of God or not.
It is better to have faith in the power of God than in the wisdom of men; it is better to trust the LORD than to put confidence in rulers.
Faith required for remission of sins.
Through faith we establish the law.
Faith necessary in the Christian warfare.
Whatever is not of faith is sin.
Faith without works is dead.
Faith necessary in prayer.
None of those who trust in the LORD shall be condemned.
To fear God is a primary duty of man.
We are commanded to fear God (you shall fear the LORD your God).
The fear of God must be constantly maintained.
The eye of the LORD is on those who fear Him.
The fear of God restrains sin.
Fear of God is necessary to the worship and service of God.
Fear not them which can kill the body, but are unable to kill the spirit; but rather fear Him who is able to destroy both spirit and body in hell. (1067 geena (gheh'- en-nah)
God will fulfill the desires of those who fear Him.
Not to fear or reverence man (for it will bring a snare upon you).
Those who fear God receive mercy and acceptance from God.
We should have a fear of God's punishment, wrath and judgment.
The fear of the LORD is the beginning of wisdom.
Awe and reverence of God is given by fear of God.
The fear of the LORD leads to life and salvation, and he who has it will not be visited with evil.
Blessings shall come to the man who fears the LORD.
There is but one God, the LORD God the Father.
You shall not have any other gods but the LORD God.
You shall not engage in idolatry and worship or serve the gods, idols or graven images of other nations.
Keep yourselves from idols.
Sorrow and shame shall come to all who hasten after another god and who boast of their idols.
are commanded to destroy all pagan idols, shrines, alters, groves, pillars, images, etc., that are in the land.
You shall not make for yourself or erect any graven image, idol, molten god, or likeness of anything to worship.
You shall not bring a graven image or other such abomination into your house.
Graven images, idols and other pagan things to be burned with fire and the material it is made out of is not to be salvaged.
It is vanity and foolish to make and worship idols or graven images.
We are not to acknowledge the gods of heathen people by making mention of their name or by swearing by them.
Death penalty is to be given to idolaters.
Those who make graven images are cursed.
Do not set up idols in your heart, for it will cause you to stumble into iniquity.
National punishment, captivity, curses and destruction for idolatry or worshiping false gods in the land.
You shall love the LORD thy God with all.thine heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy might.
God is faithful to those that love Him, and keeps His covenant and mercy with them (God acknowledges those who love Him).
God loves them that love Him.
This is the love of God, that we keep His commandments.
He that loves father or mother, son or daughter more than Christ is not worthy of Christ.
A love of worldly things is evidence of not having a love of God.
All things work together for good to them who love God.
Heed the ways of the LORD your God, for He will test you as to whether or not you love the LORD your God with all your heart and with all your soul.
We are to have a love of Christ (he who does not let him be accursed).
In order to love Christ one must obey His commandments.

We are not to allow anything to separate us from the love of God which is in Jesus Christ -not tribulation, or distress, or persecution, or famine, or nakedness, or peril, or sword, or principalities or powers.
Keep yourselves in the love of God, looking for the mercy of our Lord Jesus Christ unto eternal life.
We are required to always keep all of God's Law, His charge, His statutes, His commandments, and His judgments. Exod. .15:26;
This is God's commandment: that we should believe on the name of His Son Jesus Christ and love one another.
God loves only those who keep His commandments.
Following the Commandments of God is righteous.
We must obey Christ and his commandments.
You shall walk in all the ways of the LORD your God.
The book of the law shall not depart out of your mouth, but you shall meditate on it day and night.
We are to keep God's law continually for ever and ever.
Adhere to God's will, for He will try and prove you to see whether or not you will walk in His law and keep His commandments.

Whoever shall break one of the least of these commandments (of God), and so teaches others, shall be called least in the kingdom of God; but whoever keeps and teaches them, he shall be called great in the kingdom of heaven.
Walk orderly and keep the law.
We know God by keeping his commandments. Thus he that claims to know God but does not keep His commandments is a liar.
The law and word of God is absolute and perpetual.
Sin is the transgression of the law.
The wages of sin is death.
Where there is no law, there is no transgression.
The law gives knowledge of sin.
Obedience to the commandments of God are of prime importance in our lives.
The law of God will bring blessings if obeyed.
The Law of God will bring curses and punishment if disobeyed.
Blessings to be brought back to a people who return to obeying God's laws.
Those who forsake the law praise the wicked, but those who keep the law strive with them.

The law is not made for a righteous man, but for the lawless and disobedient, the ungodly, for sinners, for the unholy and profane, for murders, whoremongers, homosexuals, kidnappers, liars, perjurers, and whatever else is contrary to sound doctrine.
If you wish to enter into life, keep the commandments.
If you keep the commandments, you shall abide in Christ's love.
Blessed is the man who delights greatly in God's commandments.
The law has dominion over us as long as we live.
You shall not add to the word which God commanded nor take away from it.
You are not to deviate from the law to the right or to the left.
Man cannot render perfect obedience to the law (all have sinned).
We are exhorted to study the law and scriptures.
We are not to learn or follow the ways, customs or abominations of the heathen or of any ungodly nation.
We are commanded not to worship, serve or sacrifice to the gods of the heathen.
Witchcraft, wizardry, and sorcery condemned and forbidden to be practice.
Divination, soothsaying, and the use of mediums, spiritists and occultists are forbidden practices.
We are not to listen to diviners, enchanters, mediums or sorcerers.
Do not covenant with the heathen or their gods, or keep company with the heathen and idolaters.
God desires the elimination of divination from the nation.
Divination and enchantments provoke God to anger.
People are led astray and afflicted when guided by diviners instead of pastors.
We are not to sacrifice children to false gods or according to heathen practices.
You shall obey the voice of the LORD your God.
Submit yourselves to God.
Disobedience to God causes national captivity by heathen or enemy nations.
Obedience to God required by walking in His ways and by keeping His commandments.
We are to be obedient to the faith.
Blessed are those who hear the word of God and keep it.
Circumcise the foreskin of your heart, and be stiff-necked no longer.
We ought to obey God rather than men.
To him who knows to do good and does not do it, to him it is sin.
As servants of God you are to obey God.
To be obedient to God we are to be doers of His word and not hearers only.
It is not sufficient to call on the name of Christ, but to do the things which He says.
We should pray for help in turning to God from backsliding ways.
Warning not to cause or tempt others to backslide.
We are commanded to turn from evil ways and to keep God's laws and statutes.
Warnings of the iniquity of turning from God.
If a backsliding people shall humble themselves, and pray, and seek God's face, and turn from their wicked ways; then God will hear from heaven, and will forgive their sin, and will heal their land.
God is angered at those who turn their heart from Him.

When a righteous man turns away from his righteousness and commits iniquity, and does according to all the abominations that the wicked do, all the righteousness which he has done shall not be remembered.
Backsliders are exhorted to turn again back to God.
Backsliding from God's ways causes punishment and the loss of His protection.
If a people sincerely return back to God from their backsliding ways, God will bring them back from captivity, and have compassion on them.
If any will forsake the LORD and their heart turns away from Him, then His anger shall be aroused against them, and many evils and troubles shall befall them.
We should endeavor to bring back those guilty of back-sliding.
We are commanded to serve God and to hold fast to Him.
You are to serve the LORD your God with all your heart and with all your soul.
We are exhorted to worship and serve only God.
No true Christian lives or dies for himself, but lives or dies for Christ.
A faithful servant of Christ is to occupy his Kingdom.
As servants of Christ you are His freemen and thus are not to be servants of men.
True worship and service to God requires not formalism or excessive piety but to do justly, to love mercy, and to walk humbly with God.
You shall not worship the LORD your God in the manner that the heathen nations serve their gods.
A good and faithful servant of God is one that is fruitful and productive with the abilities and resources God has given him.
No man can serve two masters; You cannot serve God and wealth.
True worshipers are to worship the Father in spirit and in truth.
By serving Christ you will receive from Him the reward of the inheritance.
Blessed are those servants whom Christ shall find on the alert and doing according to his will.
You shall worship the LORD your God, and Him only you shall serve.
No man, having put his hand to the plow (to follow and serve God), and then looking back, is fit for the kingdom of God.
Serve God with a perfect heart.
Serve God in sincerity and truth.
Serve the LORD with gladness.
Serve the LORD with fear.
We are not to worship angels.
You are not to take the name of God in vain.
Cursing or blasphemy against God forbidden.
We should give no occasion for blasphemy to occur.
Blasphemy against the Holy Spirit never to be forgiven.
Whoever blasphemes the name of the LORD shall surely be put to death.
Pray to keep yourself from profaning God's name.
One blasphemes the name of God by breaking the law which he preaches others to keep.
The nation suffers from swearing.
It is a foolish people who blaspheme God's name.
Repentance commanded to all by God.
Repentance commanded by Christ.
God requires confessing of sins to Him (not to men).
Confession of sins is regarded by God through deliverance. 1. Sam. 12:10-11;
Confession and repentance necessary to pardon sin and for God to release us from His chastisements and punishments.
We are exhorted to acknowledge our transgressions and iniquity and confess them to God.
True repentance is evidenced by one's fruits.
He who covers his sins will not prosper, but whoever confesses and forsakes them will have mercy.
The word of God to be read to aid in repentance.
Confession and supplication to God required before God will release a nation from enemy infliction or captivity.
In prayer make repentance to God that He may blot out your transgressions.
Confessing of iniquities and turning from them required before God will give mercy and restore His blessings to a people.
We should repent of any uncleanness, fornication, and lasciviousness committed.
Unless you repent you will perish.
We are to give glory and praise unto God.
We should glorify God in body and spirit.
Whether you eat or drink, or whatever you do, do all to the glory of God.
Let no one glory or boast in men.
Praise should be offered to God continually.
We are to give to God the glory and praise due to his name (the LORD's name is to be praised).
Exalt the LORD our God.
Praise and exalt the name of God with song.
Punishment for not giving glory unto the name of God.
Praise God for healing received.
Glorify God to others by your good works which they may observe.
He who glories, let him glory in the LORD.
Praise and extol the LORD in the congregation of the people and among the multitude.
Prayer to God commanded.
To be close to God we must call on God.
Prayer to be continuous (without ceasing).
Prayer brings to us the things we need.
Pray for God to lead us in His righteousness.
Public prayer and worship acceptable.
Whatsoever you shall ask the Father in Christ's name, He will give it to you.
Do not be theatrical or showy when you pray, for it is better to make your prayer in secret.
Your requests and needs are to be made known to God by prayer and supplication.
We are not to have vain repetitions in prayer.
Prayers not answered to those who ask with wrong motives so as to satisfy personal pleasures.
Prayers of intercession to be made on behalf of others.
All things which you ask in prayer, believing, you shall receive.
God will not hear the prayers of a wicked people.
Prayer regarded as an abomination and rejected by God from those who hear not the law.
Be not hasty to utter anything before God, therefore it is better that your words be few.
The manner of prayer commanded by Christ (The Lord's Prayer).
Prayer to be without wrath and doubting.
Pray to be restored from backsliding.
Prayer required for forgiveness of iniquities.
We are required to give thanks to God.
With thanksgiving let your requests be made known to God.
It is a good thing to give thanks to God.
Offer thanks to Christ for guiding your life.
When we give thanks to God for what He has done in our lives, it demonstrates our faith in Him.
Give thanks to God for His indescribable gift.
Give thanks through Christ and in His name.
Give thanks in public worship and addresses.
Give thanks always for all things to God.
Give thanks upon the completion of great undertakings.
Sing songs in thanks to God for all His goodness and the wonderful works He has done.
Give thanks before taking food.
Give thanks for victory over death and the grave.
Give thanks for wisdom and might.
Give thanks for the grace and blessings bestowed on others.
Give thanks for supplying our bodily needs and other necessities.
Give thanks for nearness of God's presence.
God judges, rewards and punishes every man according to his works and deeds.
Punishment is the fruit and reward for iniquity and wicked ways (you shall reap that which you sow).
God punishes wickedness.
All who have sinned under the law will be judged by the law; but doers of the law shall be justified.
God chastises and punishes only His sons who He loves, for if you receive not chastisement, then are you bastards and not sons.
All must appear before the judgment seat of Christ, that each one may receive the things done in the body, according to what he has done, whether good or bad.
Be cautious if you walk in the ways of your heart, and in the sight of your eyes, for all these things God will bring you into judgment.
The LORD tests the righteous, but the wicked His soul hates; upon them He will rain coals, fire and brimstone and a burning wind.
Cursed be he that does not heed to all the words of the law.
Mercy triumphs over judgment.
Every one of us shall give account of himself to God.
Every idle word that men shall speak, they shall give account for it in the day of judgment. For by your words you shall be justified, and by your words you shall be condemned.
Each one's work will become manifest and revealed by fire, and the fire will test each one's work, as to what sort it is.
Each one's faith will be tried with fire.
God executes judgment here on the earth.
Rewards and punishments commence in this life.
Every man shall receive his own reward according to his own labor.
Punishment is given by disease and pestilence.
To restore the erring.
To help bear the burdens of one another.
To help those that are weak in faith.
To pray for brethren.
That which we do for our brethren we do for Christ.
Comfort each other and edify one another.
He is considered great who is servant to his brethren.
It is not good to do anything which causes your brother to stumble, or become offended, or be made weak.
We ought to lay down our lives for the brethren whom God laid down his life for.
Do unto others as you would want others to treat you.
Endure all things for the sake of the elect.
You are to forgive the trespasses of your brethren.
Forgive those you have a quarrel against as Christ forgives us.
If your brother trespass against you, rebuke him; and if he repent, forgive him.
If your brother trespass against you seven times in a day, and seven times in a day turn again to you, saying, I repent; you shall forgive him.
If any has caused sorrow, forgive and comfort him lest he be overwhelmed by the sorrow.
If you do not forgive others God will not forgive your trespasses.
Whenever you stand praying, forgive, if you have anything against anyone.
You shall love your neighbor as yourself.
Christians commanded to love one another as Christ has loved you.
Let us not love in word or in tongue, but in deed and in truth.
We should walk in and pursue love.
He that does, not love his brother does not love God, for he that loves God loves his brother also.
Through love serve one another.
He that loves not his brother abides in death and walks in darkness.
Let all that you do be done with love.
Love works no evil, and thus is the fulfilling of the law.
Let love be without hypocrisy.
We are to fervently love one another with a pure heart.
Love should be promoted and maintained.
We should be tolerant and forbearing towards one another in order to show our love.
The fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, patience, gentleness, goodness, faith.
Love covers a multitude of sins.
Open rebuke is better than love carefully concealed.
Honesty is to be provided to everyone and in all things in life you do.
We should think on honest things.
Respect what is right and honest in the sight of all men.
We are to walk honestly.
Sincerity characterizes our love to Christ.
A godly sincerity should characterize our whole conduct.
He who is near to God speaks the truth in his heart.
Dishonest gain condemned.
The preaching of the gospel to be with sincerity.
Christians exhorted to be sincere.
Those with an honest and good heart hear and keep the word of God and bring forth fruitful work.
We should pray on behalf of others that they may be sincere.
You shall not lie to one another.
Lying is iniquity and an abomination to God.
We should pray to be delivered from lying lips that speak contemptuously against the righteous.
The righteous should hate and avoid lying.
Acquiring treasures by lying is the fleeting fantasy of those who seek death.
Should not respect or keep company with those that lie.
It is better to be a poor man than a liar.
Lying is a sign of apostasy.
A lie lasts for but a moment, but truth shall be established forever.
Lying is an inherent attribute of the wicked.
Punishment and judgment for lying.
Thou shall not hate your brethren in your heart.
Wrath is a work of the flesh.
It is wicked to have hatred cloaked by deceit.
Hatred stirs up strife
Hatred is inconsistent with the ways of God.
Blessed are you, when men shall hate you, and ostracized you, insult you, and spurn your name as evil, for the sake of Christ.
Let none of you think evil in your heart against your neighbor.
Whosoever is angry with his brother without cause shall be in danger of judgment.
Show no malice nor desire ill will towards your brethren.
Christian growth requires that you set aside all malice and guile.
Malice works as leaven and is incompatible with sincerity and truth.
There is a time to hate.
Christian liberty is not to be made a cloak for maliciousness.
We should hate those that hate God.
A servant of God is to be gentle to all men.
Christians to be in fellowship with one another.
We should have fellowship in the gospel.
We should serve one another.
We are not to consent with sinners and evildoers, or walk with them, or sit down with them.
Do not be unequally yoked together with unbelievers; for what fellowship has righteousness with unrighteousness? And what communion has light with darkness.
Where two or three are gathered in Christ's name, He is there in the midst of them.
We are not to have fellowship with unfruitful works of darkness.
Bad company corrupts good habits and morals.
Christians are to work together each using their specific talents, abilities and ministries as one body, working towards God's will and His kingdom - For we are God's fellow workers.
We are to be like-minded with one another according to Christ Jesus, that we may with one mind glorify God.
If any come to you who do not have the doctrine of Christ, do not receive him into your house nor greet him.
Blessed is the man who walks not in the counsel of the ungodly.
It is good and pleasant for brethren to dwell together in unity.
With unity and fellowship comes strength, advantages, and benefits.
Do not keep company with fornicators, extortioners, the covetous, idolaters, slanderers, revilers, drunkards or the wicked, or brethren who walk contrary to God.
If we walk in the light as Christ is in the light, we have fellowship with one another.
Do not associate with a man given to anger, or go with a hot-tempered man, lest you learn his ways.
Unity exhorted by being like-minded one toward another according to Jesus Christ.
Flatter is not godly and is not to be used.
Do not associate with those that use flattery.
Speak not with flattering words so as to please men but rather please God who tries our heart.
Flattery is a corrupting influence.
Beware of those who speak many words, flattering people to gain advantage.
Punishment for flattery.
Flattery is a snare to those that use it.
A flattering mouth brings ruin.
Rejoice not at the misfortunes of your adversaries.
We are to love our personal adversaries.
Pray for and forgive those that hate and persecute you.
Do not desire the death of your adversaries.
We are not to curse adversaries.
Do not hastily strive with your neighbor, but discuss your cause with him.
Do not strive with a man without cause.

Christians exhorted to avoid foolish and ignorant disputes over words, fables, unlearned questions, or matters about the law or genealogies that give rise to mere speculation, knowing that they generate strife, envy, abusive language and evil suspicions.
The LORD hates him that sows discord among brethren.
Withdraw from disputings between men of corrupt minds, who are destitute of the truth, and suppose godliness is a means of gain.
Strife in your heart is dishonorable.
Pride is a cause of strife and contention.
Do not grumble and complain against one another, lest you be condemned.
We should do all that is possible to avoid strife between brethren.
Christians are not to walk in strife.
We are to avoid those who cause divisions and offenses contrary to biblical doctrine.
You are not to act out of strife but do all things without disputing.
Christians should submit to a petty assault or wrong rather than engage in strife and conflict (should turn the other cheek).
A wrathful man stirs up strife, but he who is slow to anger pacifies contention.
We should seek God's protection from strife and conflict.
It is honorable for a man to stop striving, since any fool can start a quarrel.
We should praise God for delivering and protecting us from strife.
If your adversary is hungry, feed him; if he thirst, give him drink: for in so doing you shall heap burning coals upon his head.
Strife is a work of the flesh.
It is a fool's lips that start contentions.
Strife leads to confusion and every evil work.
Promoters of strife should be expelled.
The beginning of strife is like releasing water; therefore stop contention before a quarrel starts.
We are forbidden to defraud our neighbor or brethren.
No one should defraud his brother regarding the matter of lust and sexual immorality.
Do not let those who work deceit dwell within your house.
Deceive not with your lips.
Beware of those that serve not our Lord Jesus Christ, for by their good words and flattering speech they deceive the hearts of the unsuspecting.
You shall not deal falsely or treacherously with your brethren.
You shall not keep back the wages due a hired laborer by fraud.
Deceit is falsehood.
Keep your lips from speaking guile.
Take heed that no man deceive you regarding the Gospel.
God abhors a deceitful man.
Deceit and fraud a characteristic of the wicked.
The saints are to be free from deceit and avoid such practices.
Let no one deceive you by any means that would cause you to depart from the faith.
Punishment will come to those who attempt to gain by deceit.
Deceive not yourself regarding the ways and prophesies of God.
We are exhorted to sympathize with other Christians.
Having compassion can make a difference.
We should exercise compassion and pity towards the afflicted.
Have compassion for the poor.
Compassion and aid to be given to one that is found hurt and injured and robbed.
Have compassion and pity for one another.
Be merciful, just as your Father is merciful.
Show mercy and compassion everyone to his brother.
To him that is afflicted, pity should be shown from his friend.
Trespasses are to be first taken to the transgressor for him to remedy his fault.
If your brother trespass against you, rebuke him; and if he repent, forgive him.
We should reprove and admonish one another to prevent sin.
We should receive reproof kindly.
Have no fellowship with the unfruitful works of darkness, but rather reprove them.
Do not judge others lest you be judged yourselves, for in the way you judge, you will be judged.
Hatred and rejection of reproof of one's faults leads to error, ignorance, remorse and destruction.
Reprove one another that there be no strife or contentions.
Do not reprove and correct others of their ignorance and blindness when you suffer from the same affliction.
He who rebukes a man will find more favor afterward than he who flatters with the tongue.
Admonish those who are unruly.
Reproofs of instruction are the way of life.
Reject a heretick and factious man after the first and second admonition, knowing that such a man is perverted and lost in sin, being self-condemned.
If a brethren is in fault then restore him in a spirit of meekness.
Do not reprove a fool or a scoffer, lest he hate you, for reprove is more effective for a wise man, and he also will love you for it.
You should not refuse to be corrected and reproved by the righteous among you.
Confess your faults to one another.
You are to forgive one another if any one have a quarrel against you.
In meekness instruct and correct those who are in opposition, for perhaps God may give them a change of mind towards an acknowledgment of the truth.
We are exhorted to reprove, rebuke and correct with authority, patience and instruction.
He who heeds reproof gets understanding, and will abide among the wise.
The laws, statutes, commandments and judgments of God are to be kept throughout the land.
There is to be one law applied to the citizen and the stranger.
Foreigners to abide by and obey God's law.
The LORD is our lawgiver.
You shall not follow the laws and ordinances of other nations in your land.
He who does any thing defiantly and with contempt for the law, that person shall be cut off from among his people.
All must confirm the words of the law by doing them.
Laws and decrees that are contrary to Divine law or justice, or oppress the rights of persons, are repugnant and void.
We are to remember the ancient events and principles of the past which formed the law of the land.
The law is to be revealed to the people; it is not to be kept secret, or made obscure, or hidden in any manner.
The law is to be publicly written, displayed and recorded.
Every seven years, on the year of release, the law is to be read before all the people that they may learn and observe all the words of the law.
The Law is to be taught and instructed privately and publicly.
The law is to be displayed on door posts of homes and on city gates.
The law is to be publicly read to remind the people of the law and that it is to be observed.
You are not to take a gift or money offered as a bribe.
Bribery condemned as being wicked and perverting justice and judgment.
He who takes a bribe against the innocent may not dwell in the LORD's holy nation.
You shall not take a bribe, for a bribe blinds the wise and subverts the cause of the just.
Those in government who take bribes overthrows the justice and stability established in the land.
They are cursed who take reward against the innocent.
He that hates gifts is blessed.
It is iniquity for judges to pronounce judgment for a bribe or reward.
If you swear or take an oath you shall do so in God's name.
You shall make no false or deceitful oath or covenant.
You shall not swear by God's name falsely.
When one fully performs all the terms of an oath or contract, he is clear of all obligation to it.
If a man makes a vow to God or swears an oath to bind himself by contract or binding obligation, he shall not violate his word but shall do all that he stated.
You are to keep your word.
When you make a vow unto God, you shall not delay to pay it, for God will require you to keep your word.
If you refrain from vowing there is no sin in not performing what you said you would do.
If a young woman, who is under her father's house, makes a vow and her father hears it but says nothing then all her vows shall stand.
A father can cancel the obligations of a vow or contract by his daughter who is in his house.
A husband can allow or annul the vows or contracts made by his wife.
A vow of a widow or divorced woman shall stand against her.
If a divorced woman makes a vow while in her husband's house, her husband can affirm or annul the vow.
We should avoid making any oaths so that you may not fall under judgment.
God will judge and punish false swearers.

If a person swears thoughtlessly with his lips to do evil or to do good, and whatever he pronounced by the oath is hidden or unknown to him, when he comes to know it, then he shall be guilty in these matters and shall confess them.
You shall not bear false witness against another nor raise a false report.
A faithful witness speaks the truth and saves lives, but a false witness speaks lies.
One witness shall not condemn a man for any iniquity or crime he commits.
Do not join your hand with a wicked man to be an unrighteous witness.
False witness is an abomination and condemned.
Do not be a witness against your neighbor without cause.
A false witness is to be punished.
Physical proofs and facts can serve as a witness or evidence in certain cases.
You shall not testify in a dispute for the sake of following the majority and thus pervert justice.
At the testimony of two or three witnesses shall the fact of the matter be established.
We are not to be a witness against another without cause.
If someone gives contrary testimony, then the judges shall make diligent inquisition between both men to see if the witness is a false witness.
If a witness is found to be a false witness by testifying falsely against his brother, then he shall receive the punishment that the accused brethren would have received if guilty.
When a person who is a witness sins when he has taken an oath, about an event he saw or knew, if he does not tell it, then he will bear his guilt.
A disreputable witness scorns justice.
You are not to twist, distort or pervert justice.
You shall not be unjust but shall follow that which is just and righteous in matters of law and judgment.
You are not to be partial towards anyone or a respecter of persons in exacting justice, whether they be poor or rich, small or great.
Judgment to be quickly executed upon those violating the law of God or the law of the land.
Seek good, and not evil; hate the evil, and love the good, and establish justice in your courts.
You shall keep far from a false matter.
Injustice of the least kind is condemned.
You shall do no injustice regarding the measurement of length, weight or volume, but shall adhere to a just and standard measurement.
They are condemned who call evil good, and good evil.
We are commanded to act justly and pursue justice.
You shall not pervert the judgment of the stranger, the widow, the oppressed nor of the fatherless.
You shall not pervert judgment of the poor or needy in his cause but judge them righteously and deliver them out of the hand of the wicked.
Doing injustice by justifying the wicked and condemning the righteous is an abomination and condemned by God.
Blessed are those who keep justice.
Punishment required for injustice.
You shall not turn aside the needy from judgment, or take away the rights from the poor by unrighteous decrees.
When the wicked surround the righteous, the law becomes ignored, justice is never upheld, and wrong judgment is rendered.
Marriage between man and woman is instituted by God as a good and natural thing.
Husband and wife are to remain together for life (marriage vows to be kept).
A woman is bound by the law to her husband so long as he lives; but if the husband dies, she is released from the law concerning the husband.
Husband and wife regarded as one flesh. Gen, 2:23-24;
Marriage is honorable among all, and the bed undefiled.
Husband and wife are to have children (be fruitful and multiply).
Marriage bonds are of God and not to be put asunder by any man.
Man is not independent of woman, nor is woman independent of man.
Husbands are to have authority over their wives.
A husband is to live with his wife in an understanding way, and give honor and respect to her.
Husbands are to love their wives and be not bitter against them.
A husband is to be faithful to his wife.
Husbands are to be satisfied with their wives.
Let the husband render to his wife due benevolence or affection.
Husband to provide for the family.
Wives are to obey their husband.
Wife is to remain with her husband for life.
Wives to be in subjection to their husbands.
The wife is to take care of the house and family needs.
Wives are to be modest, chaste, discreet and sober.
Wife not to usurp authority over the man.
The wife is not to raise questions in the church but to ask through her husband.
Wives are to render due benevolence or affection to her husband.
A wife is to be virtuous.
Wife is to love her husband and children.
A woman of valor is the crown of her husband, but she who shames him is as rottenness in his bones.
Wife is to reverence her husband.
Wife is to be faithful to her husband.
Wives are to love their children.
To lie carnally with another man's wife is forbidden.
Whosoever divorces his wife and marries another woman commits adultery.
If a woman divorces her husband and marries another man she commits adultery.
For an engaged woman to have sex with another man is to be considered as adultery.
Adultery not to be committed in the heart.
Instances of Adultery. 2 Sam. 11 , etc.;
A childless widow is not to marry a stranger, but rather the brother of her dead husband.
Marriage of a divorced woman is adultery.
Procedure regarding a jealous husband who believes his wife has been unfaithful and gone astray to defile herself with another man.
God will judge adulterers.
It is the will of God that you abstain from fornication and sexual immorality.
A woman married who is believed to be a virgin and found out not to be, shall be stoned to death for playing the whore in her father's house.
If a man entices a woman not engaged, and lies with her, he must endow her to be his wife.
To avoid fornication, let every man have his own wife, and every woman her own husband.
There shall be no whore of the daughters of Israel.
law does not sanction fornication. 1 Tim. 1:9-10. God will judge the sexually immoral acts of persons.
Fornication is ruinous.
You shall not approach a woman unclean by menstruation to uncover her sexuality and lie with her.
We are not to associate with fornicators.
Repent of any fornication committed.
One should not depart from their spouse.
We should not separate from our spouse because of their disbelief.
A bill of divorce can be written when some uncleanness is found in a woman recently married.
Divorce of a wife permitted for her act of fornication.
If a man divorces his wife and marries another he commits adultery against her.
If a woman divorces her husband and marries another she commits adultery.
A woman, even if divorced, cannot marry another man as long as her husband is alive.
A man or a woman is not bound to an unbelieving mate that departs.
With father or mother.
With one's sister or half-sister.
With one's mother-in-law.
With a grandchild.
With one's aunt.
With one's uncle or uncle's wife.
With one's daughter-in-law.
With your brother's wife.
With a woman and her daughter or her grand daughter.
With two women who are sisters.
With thy neighbor's wife.
We are not to intermarry with those who practice idolatry.
We are not to marry unbelievers.
We are not to marry those of other races.
Children are a gift and heritage from God, and thus are to be asked of from God.
Parents are to love their children.
Parents should pray for and bless their children.
Parents should sternly chastise and punish their children to put them on a righteous course - For he who spares the rod hates his son, but he who loves his son disciplines him diligently.
Father to have authority over children.
The head of the house is to provide for the family.
Parents are responsible to save up for their children's future.
Fathers are not to provoke children to anger.
Mothers are to be concerned about the ways of their household.
The sins of the fathers are visited on their children to the third and fourth generation.
Children are to obey and listen to their parents.
Children to honor their father and mother.
Everyone shall fear (reverence) his mother and his father.
Children are to hear the instruction of their father, and forsake not the law of their mother.
A wise son makes a father glad, but a foolish son is a grief to his mother and father.
Children shall not rob their father or mother.
Children are to take care of their parents.
Children are not to curse their parents.
A child that is rebellious and who refuses to obey his parents is to be put to death.
Cursed is the one who treats his father or his mother with contempt.
Children that curse their father or mother are to be put to death.
Children that strike their father or mother are to be put to death.
It is a sin for children to rob parents.
He who mistreats his father, and drives away his mother, is a son who brings shame and disgrace.
Condemnation offered to he who mocks his father and scorns his mother.
Parents should see that children are educated and instructed in the ways and laws of God.
Children to be taught to fear God.
Bible stories and illustrations, and the works of God, are to be taught to each generation.
Train up a child in the way he should go, and when he is old, he will not depart from it.
Education to be by right examples.
Reproofs for discipline to be given to the young to keep them from immoral temptations and lusts.
Firstborn son is to receive the father's birthright.
Illegitimate children not to receive birthright.
Blessings to be bestowed on the heir of the family.
Birthright of the firstborn can be sold to another son .
A greater portion of the father's inheritance to be given to the firstborn son.
Primary part of inheritance to go to firstborn son rather than a favored son.
Houses and riches are given as an inheritance from a father.
Land ownership can pass by inheritance.
A good man leaves an inheritance to his children's children.
Daughters are to receive an inheritance from their father when he has no son.
If a man has no children his inheritance is given to his brothers.
If a man has no children or brothers then his inheritance is given to his father's brethren or his nearest family kin.
Birthright of firstborn son can be lost and given up to another son if the firstborn commits a sin against the family.

When a man dies having no children and his widow marries her husband's brother, the son she bears by him shall succeed in the name of the brother which is dead and shall have his birthright and inheritance.
A will and testament is in force after a man is dead, for it is never in force while the one who made it lives.
A heir, as long as he is a child, is under guardians until the time prescribed by his father that he is to inherit.
You are not to work animals on the Sabbath.
You are not to have two different kinds of animals work together; You shall not plow with an ox and an ass together.
You shall not muzzle the mouth of the ox that is being used for work.
If an animal kills a person the animal is to be put to death.

If an animal is proven to be aggressive, and its owner has been warned, yet he does not confine it, and it kills a man or woman, then both the animal and the owner are to be put to death. If there is a ransom of money demanded of the owner, it can be paid for the redemption of his life.
If an animal shall gore a servant, the owner shall give the servant's master a set amount of money and the animal is to be killed.
If a man's animal eats the crop of another man's field, he shall make restitution from the best of his own field.
If one man's animal kills another's animal, then the live animal shall be sold and the money (and the dead animal if it be cattle) shall be divided between them.
If an animal which is known to be aggressive kills another animal yet its owner had not confined him, then he shall pay for the animal killed but can keep the dead animal.
Stolen animals are to be repaid to the owner 4 or 5 times.
Stray animals belonging to your brethren are be brought back to the owner. If the owner is unknown, then you are to keep the animal until the owner comes looking for it and then return it to him.
If you encounter an animal of your enemy going astray, you shall bring it back to him.
If a pit is opened or dug and left uncovered, and an animal falls into it, the owner of the pit shall pay the owner of the animal but he can keep the dead animal.
If you see an animal of one that hates you lying helpless under its load, you shall release the animal.
You shall not see your brother's ass or ox fall down by the way, and hide yourself from them: you shall surely help him to lift them up again.
Whoever kills another's animal shall make it good, animal for animal.

If a man gives his neighbor his animal to keep for him and it dies or runs away, then an oath before the LORD shall be made between them, that he has not laid his hands on his neighbor's animal. He is not required to pay for it.
If a borrowed animal is stolen, the keeper shall make restitution to the owner of the animal.
If a borrowed animal is torn in pieces, the remains shall be brought as evidence, and no restitution shall be made.
If a man borrows any animal, and it is injured or dies while its owner is not with it, he shall make full restitution to the owner. But if the owner is with it, no restitution is to be made.
You are not to breed cattle with a diverse kind (no hybrid cattle, livestock or pets).
Should have regard for the life of your animals.
Do not separate a newly born ox or sheep or a goat from its mother for the first seven days.
The eggs or young can be taken from a bird's nest but not along with the mother.
Know well the condition of your flocks, and pay attention to your herds.
Leaders chosen must be wise and just.
Civil leaders are to be diligent in governing.
Civil leaders are to be men of truth, hating covetousness.
Civil leaders, judges and officers are to fear God.
Civil leaders are to be of God.
Rulers are not to be a terror to good behavior, but rather to the wicked and evil doers.
Civil rulers are not to use their office and position to bring gain to themselves.
Civil rulers are ministers of God for good.
Irresponsible civil leaders are they who are either blind, ignorant, lazy, greedy, self-centered, drunkards, or act for their own gain.
Civil rulers are to record, preserve, study and proclaim the law of God at all times.
If a ruler unintentionally or out of ignorance violates the law and the violation comes to his knowledge, he shall make restitution for it.
Civil leaders and authorities are to be men not women.

Government officers are to execute judgment and righteousness, and deliver the spoiled out of the hand of the oppressor; they are to do no wrong, do no violence to the stranger, the fatherless, nor the widow, neither shed innocent blood in the land.
Government officers that engage in conspiracy, treachery and murder are to be put to death.
The Law of God is to be read in public addresses by civil leaders to direct the course of society and government.
A good civil leader or judge is from God, and keeps a people from rebelling against the ways of God.
Civil authorities who are oppressive do not understand justice.
Lying is unbecoming in rulers.
If a ruler hearken to lies, all his aides and ministers become wicked.
Those in government are not to consult mediums or spiritists for guidance but are to inquire of the LORD.
Civil leaders are not to drink lest it causes them to forget the law and pervert justice.
Civil rulers are to be chosen from among thy brethren or race, we are not to put a stranger (an alien or one of another race) over us in a position of authority.
God will punish civil authorities who punish unjustly and contrary to the law.
It is an abomination for a civil ruler to commit wickedness, for his office is established on righteousness.
The powers of government are appointed by God and are in His hand.
A distribution of power and levels of authority are to be established-rulers of thousands, and rulers of hundreds, rulers of fifties, and rulers of tens.
Judges, magistrates and officers are to be appointed in all towns and cities.
The less wicked a government is, the more the righteous will prosper.
Government is to be for the punishment of the evildoers, and for the praise of them that do well.
Warnings against an all-powerful leader, king or central government.
When the righteous are in authority, the people rejoice: but when the wicked bear rule, the people mourn.
Government officials are to be chosen by the people.
When the wicked are removed from the presence of civil leaders, the government will be established in righteousness.
Judges were originally established by God.
Judges shall justify the righteous and condemn the wicked.
Judges shall righteously judge the causes and transgressions between persons with just judgment.
Judges are not to be partial or respect persons in judgment, but shall equally judge the small as well as the great.
Judges are not to take a gift or bribe.
Judges are to judge the people at all times.
Judges and magistrates are to know the laws of God.
Judges judge not for man but for God.
The judge that justifies the wicked and condemns the just is an abomination to God.
Wisdom and knowledge is needed and should be prayed for in order to judge between good and bad.
Judges are to judge matters according to the laws, statutes, commandments, and judgments of God.
We should respect and give obedience to rulers and authorities who preside as God's ministers.
Disobedience to government is justified when government requires an ungodly or unlawful act.
We should pray for civil leaders.
It is not proper to despise government.
Rebellion is justified by oppressive laws and taxes.
We should disregard laws prohibiting the gospel.
We should not rebel or cause insurrection against the established government.
You shall not curse or speak evil of civil rulers or dignitaries.
Submit to them that have civil authority.
We are not to submit to human edicts when in conflict with Divine laws.
Passover is to be observed.
The Passover is to be a solemn observance throughout all generations.
No outsider, sojourner or hired servant shall eat of the Passover meal.
Those unable to keep the Passover at its proper time are to keep it one month later.
The Feast of Unleavened Bread is to be celebrated the day after Passover (to eat unleavened bread seven days)
Wave Sheaf offering (2nd day after Passover).
In the first and seventh day of the Feast of Unleavened Bread there shall be an holy convocation, you shall do no servile work.
The Feast of Harvest (the first-fruits of thy labor).
The Feast of Ingathering.
Feast of Weeks (Pentecost) -Seven weeks to be counted from the time you begin harvest, then on the fiftieth day you shall celebrate the Feast of Weeks.
Feast of Trumpets -a day for blowing the trumpets (To do no work on that day).
Feast of Tabernacles -you shall keep a feast to the LORD for seven days.
You shall celebrate the Feast of Tabernacles seven days after you have gathered in from your threshing floor and wine vat.
On the first and eighth day of the Feast of Tabernacles you shall have a sacred assembly, you shall do no customary work.
Day of Atonement - You shall humble your souls and do no work on that day.
Anointing (inauguration ceremony) for new civil leader coming into office.
The first born of man or animal to be dedicated to God.
Three times in a year all males shall appear before the God of Israel, and make an offering to provide for the feasts.
Be baptized every one of you in the name of Jesus Christ for the remission of sins.
Feasts to be published and proclaimed in all the cities and towns in the land.
Partaking of Communion in remembrance of Christ and in celebration of the Lord's supper.
The Sabbath as a time of rest from work was instituted by God.
The Sabbath to be kept holy.

Six days of the week are to be used for labor, and the seventh day to be a Sabbath of rest in which you shall do no work. Exod. 16:22-30; Exod. 20:9-11; Exod. 23:12; Exod. 31:15; Exod. 34:21; Exod. 35:2; Lev, 23:3;
Sabbaths commanded to be kept.
Keeping the Sabbath is a sign of a covenant with God.
No buying, selling or marketing is to transpire on the Sabbath.
No house work to be done on the Sabbath.
No burdens to be carried on during the Sabbath.
The Sabbath was made for man, and not man for the Sabbath.
Christ is Lord of the Sabbath.
Provide for food needed on the Sabbath in advance so it need not be gathered or bought or cooked on the Sabbath.
We are not to seek our own pleasure on the Sabbath.
Divine worship to be celebrated on the Sabbath (a time for holy convocation).
The Scriptures to be read to the people on the Sabbath day.
Works connected with religious service are lawful on the Sabbath.
Good deeds and works of mercy are lawful on the Sabbath.
Acts needed to sustain life may be performed on the Sabbath.
Acts of necessity may be performed on the Sabbath.
You honor God in observing the Sabbath.
Six years you shall sow the land and reap its produce, but the seventh year you shall let the land lie fallow.
Every seventh year to be a Sabbath of rest for the land, you shall neither sow your field nor prune your vineyard.
In the year of the land Sabbath you are not to harvest those crops which grow by its own accord.
The food which grows of itself can be taken by the poor to eat during the land Sabbath.
Food requirement for the year of the land Sabbath and following year will be provided by God with an abundant crop in the sixth year.
The land and its fruits are holy to God, and therefore should not be abused.
A Jubilee is to be observed at the end of every seven land Sabbaths (every fifty years).
The fiftieth year or the Jubilee is to be hallowed and to be a year of liberty and release throughout the land.
You shall not sow or reap on the Jubilee year but eat the increase gathered in previous years.
The Jubilee to be holy to you.
On the year of the Jubilee you shall return to every man his property, the field shall return to the one from whom it was purchased, to whom the possession of the land belongs.
All those in service to another are to be released from their contract or indenture of service, and allowed to return to his family.
The Jubilee to start and be proclaimed on the Day of Atonement.
Thou shall not murder.
Shedding of innocent blood is an abomination to God.
God requires the blood of a murderer for it defiles the land.
Those guilty of murder are to be put to death.
If a man acts with premeditation against his neighbor, to kill him with guile, he shall die.
One who strikes a man so that he dies is a murderer and shall be put to death.
Killing for hire is condemned (the assassin and the one who hires him are both guilty of murder).
You are not to act against the life of your neighbor.
The law concerning unsolved murders.
Every one that defiles the Sabbath by doing servile work on that day shall be put to death.
He that kidnaps a man, whether he sells him or he is found in his possession, he shall be put to death.
A man or a woman with a familiar spirit or who is a wizard shall be put to death.
You are not to allow a witch or sorceress to live.
He that strikes his father or mother shall be put to death.
He that curses his father or mother shall be put to death.
If a man have a stubborn and rebellious son which will not obey the voice of his parents, and when they chastise him, he will not listen to them, he shall then be put to death.
Anyone that has served or worshipped false or pagan gods shall be put to death.
Idolaters are to be destroyed.
A preacher or a prophet who leads people to worship false gods is to be put to death, because he has counseled rebel against God.
Those who entice others to serve pagan gods and religions are to be put to death.
He that blasphemes the name of God shall be put to death.
He that sacrifices to any god, other than the LORD God alone, shall be utterly destroyed.
Whoever rebels against the laws of the land shall be put to death.
The man that acts presumptuously by not listening to the priest or the judges, that man shall die.
Rebellion and insurrection against the government is punishable by death.
Any that offer their children to pagan gods shall be put to death.
Curses brought upon a nation that allows child sacrifice in its land.
You shall not let any of your offspring pass through the fire of Molech.
Manslaughter or accidental killing is not punished by death, but the one guilty is to be banished to a city of refuge.
If the manslayer at any time goes outside the city of refuge where he fled, he is subject to be killed by the avenger of blood.
If a murder flees to a city of refuge, he is to be turned over to the hand of the executioner that he may die.
The adulterer and adulteress are to be put to death.
Sexual relations to affinity of blood that require death.
Those guilty of sodomy (homosexuality) to be put to death.
The act of sodomy condemned as an abomination and an unnatural act.
Sodomites are not allowed to exist in the nation.
Those having sexual relations with animals are to be put to death.
Whores or prostitutes are to be put to death.
If a virgin betrothed to a husband lie with another man, both the man and woman shall be put to death.
A rapist is to be put to death.
We are to pray for deliverance from our enemies.
Overcome enemies by kindness.
Christ's enemies are to be destroyed.
We are not to help ungodly and anti-Christ nations or show friendship towards them.
We can lend to other nations but are not to borrow from them.
It is vain to rely on other nations for help while ignoring the aid of God.
Alliances and covenants (treaties) with pagan or ungodly nations are forbidden.
Covenants with pagan or ungodly nations leads to idolatry and adoption of pagan ways.
Do not to follow the ways of other nations.
A treaty of peace, agreeing to do no harm to another friendly nation, can be enacted.
Alliances made with wicked nations will not be fruitful.
We should make an effort, and do what is reasonably possible, to avoid strife and contention (and possible war) with other nations.
International trade, and importing and exporting of goods, can be conducted.
Iniquity in trading is condemned.
Ambassadors can be sent to foreign nations to convey messages to it and to speak on behave of the government.
You shall not allow foreigners that are pagans to emigrate into or dwell in your nation; for they shall be as pricks in your eyes and as thorns in your sides, and they shall trouble you in your land.
Do not render evil to a nation at peace with you.
When in a foreign nation, you may buy and sell with it but meddle not in its affairs.
Chastity commanded; and that you not to be fornicators.
We should be chaste in the heart.
We are to keep the body in chastity.
Chastity is preserved by wisdom and discretion.
We should not keep company with those devoid of chastity.
Keep yourself pure in mind and heart.
Immoral and unchaste conduct (works of the flesh) excludes entry into the Kingdom of God.
Abstain and turn away from every form of evil.
A virtuous person should let their mind dwell on those things which are true, honorable, just, pure, lovely, and of good report.
It is chaste to add virtue in your faith and knowledge to virtue.
Virtue in women is a highly desired attribute.
A gracious woman retains honor.
You shall do what is right and good in the sight of the LORD, that it may be well with you.
As a ring of gold in a swine's snout, so is a beautiful woman who lacks discretion.
Whoredom and prostitution is forbidden.
Whoremongers condemned.
To the pure all things are pure, but to those who are defiled and unbelieving nothing is pure.
Punishment and consequences for breach of chaste conduct.
Seek good and not evil; hate evil, love good.
Busybodies exhorted to mind their own business.
Christians exhorted not to suffer as a consequence of being a meddler in other people's matters.
We are not to wander from house to house as tattlers and busybodies.
We should not meddle in other's concerns.
Gossiping is not proper and a sign of a depraved mind.
Every fool will be meddling.
We are admonished not to gossip.
We should not talk about the errors or transgressions of others.
Gossip often arises from hatred.
Gossip causes a separation in friendship.
Do not associate with a gossip.
Where gossiping is eliminated, strife ceases.
Seeking pleasures and lavish living is not Godly.
Lovers of pleasure are brought into poverty.
To seek mirth and pleasure is vanity.
Beware of those who are lovers of pleasure rather than lovers of God.
We should display moderation.
Gluttony and excessiveness is iniquity and leads to a carnal outlook on life.
It is wise to abstain from indulgences.
Avoid lasciviousness and wantonness or covetousness.
We are not to desire riches.
Indulgence is a proof of folly.
Women shall not wear men's clothing, nor shall a man put on women's clothing, this is an abomination to God.
We are not to wear a garment of mixed fabrics (e.g. wool and linen).
Women are to wear modest apparel and should not have braided hair or adorn themselves with gold or fancy and costly array.
Clothes are to be washed before appearing in the sight of God.
Whoever handles the carcass of unclean animals is to wash their clothes.
Long hair is a shame for men.
Long hair is a glory for women.
Nakedness is condemned.
Slander and speaking lies about your brethren is an abomination to God.
You shall not go about speaking slander or spreading false reports about others.
You shall not backbite others.
A backbiting tongue brings forth an angry countenance (no one will be pleased with a backbiter).
A talebearer who spreads scandals causes harm to others.
He who does not backbite and slander with his tongue is near to God.
We should not speak evil of someone out of suspicions or assumptions.
Beware of those who are slanderers.
Slander is a characteristic of the wicked.
Libel and name calling is condemned by Christ.
He that speaks slander is a fool.
Those who indulge in slander are not to be trusted.
Slander is a sign of a debauched and corrupt people.
We are commanded to put away all such evil speaking.
You shall not go about as a slanderer among your people.
You are to speak evil of no man.
He who secretly slanders his neighbor is to be cut off from the people.
We are exhorted to be courteous.
Be peaceable, well behaved, showing courtesy and every consideration to all men.
Brotherly kindness is needed to be fruitful in the knowledge of Jesus Christ.
We are to show kindness to one another.
Sobriety commanded.
The gospel teaches we should live soberly.
The taking of wine or strong drink is forbidden when going into the tabernacle of the congregation.
Those in the service of God are not to drink alcohol.
Drinking and Drunkenness not approved.
Drinking and merrymaking prevents the people from seeing the afflictions of the nation.
Excessive or habitual drinking is admonished against, as it causes a disregard of the judgments and works of God.
Pregnant women are not to take alcoholic drinks.
Intoxicating drink causes persons to err and be led astray.
We are not to associate with those that are drunkards and gluttons.
Addiction to intoxicating drink brings sorrow, contentions, complaints, wounds without cause, and redness of eyes.
Wine is a mocker, strong drink arouses brawling, and whoever is intoxicated by it is deluded and not wise.
You are not to encourage another to drink or attempt to get another drunk.
Whatever work you put your hands to, do it with all your might.
Every man should enjoy the good of all his labor.
The laborer is worthy of his hire (wages).
We are exhorted to walk in a manner worthy of the vocation with which we have been called.
Every man shall receive his own reward according to his own labor.
If any would not work, neither should he eat.
Lead a quite life, mind your own business, and work with your own hands.
Be not slothful in business, but be fervent in spirit.
Do not engage in work and labor that is vain or futile.
For wealth -In all labor there is profit.
Wealth gotten by vanity shall be diminished; but he that gathers by labor shall increase.
To reduce crime - Let him who stole steal no more: but rather let him labor, working with his hands.
To satisfy hunger - A person who labors, labors for himself, for his hunger urges him on.
An idle man shall suffer hunger.
In the sweat of thy face shall you eat bread.
All the labor of man is for his mouth.
To prevent poverty - He becomes poor that deals with a slack hand; but the hand of the diligent makes one rich.
Love not sleep, lest you come to poverty.
For life - the labor of the righteous leads to life.
To cause productivity rather than waste - He who is slack in his work is brother to him who destroys.
A man who is diligent in his business will stand before kings, and not the lowly.
To have a peaceful life - The sleep of a laboring man is sweet, whether he eat little or much; but the abundance of the rich will not suffer him to sleep.
A hard-working farmer ought to be the first to partake of his crops.
He that sows sparingly shall also reap sparingly; and he which sows bountifully shall also reap bountifully.
The sluggard will not plow by reason of the cold; therefore shall he beg in harvest, and have nothing.
He that tills his land shall have plenty of bread; but he that follows after vain persons shall have poverty.
You shall eat the labor of your hands, and it shall be well with you.
The fields of the slothful will be overgrown with thistles and weeds, his farm broken down, and he will fall into poverty.
Be not overly concerned about the weather when you sow and reap, for you do not know the works of God.
We are to be doers of God's word, and not just hearers of it.
Commit your works to the LORD, and your thoughts will be established.
Unless the LORD builds the house, they labor in vain who build it.
Be steadfast, immovable, always abounding in the works of the Lord, knowing that your labor is not in vain in the Lord.
Whatever animals that have divided or cloven hoofs and chews its cud you may eat.
Fishes that have fins and scales may be eaten (Bass, croppie, flounder, cod, haddock, pike, salmon, sunfish, mackerel, snapper, trout, perch, smelt, tuna, etc.).
All clean birds can be eaten (e.g., chicken, turkey, pheasant, quail, grouse, partridge, etc.).
Insects-locust, bald locust, grasshoppers.
If a clean animal dies it is considered unclean until evening.
Animals which you can eat--ox, sheep, goats, deer, roebuck, gazelle, fallow deer, wild goat, antelope, buffalo, caribou, elk, ibex, wild ox, moose, chamois.
Camel (does not have a divided hoof).
Rabbits, hares, and rock hyrax (does not have a divided hoof).
Cattle which either do not chew the cud or divide the hoof (horse, donkey, quagga, llama, etc.).
Swine or hog (does not chew the cud).
Creeping things-weasel, mouse, tortoise, turtle, sand reptile, ferret, chameleon, gecko, frogs, toads, snakes, crocodile, lizard, squirrel, raccoon, mole.
All water life that does not have fins and scales are not to be eaten (e.g., shrimp, lobster, snails, clams, shark, shell fish, eels, catfish, scallop, octopus, etc.).
Every creeping thing that flies is unclean.

Unclean birds-Eagle, buzzard, osprey, vultures, kite, ravens, owl, night hawk, ostrich, hawk, little owl, cormorant, great owl, falcon, swan, pelican, stork, herons, hoopoe, bats (and the eggs of unclean birds).
All winged insects that walk on all fours.
Whatever crawls upon its belly or is multi-footed among all creeping things that creep on the earth.
Whatever goes on its paws, among all kinds of animals that go on all fours, are unclean (e.g., dogs, cats, coyote, bears, foxes, etc.).
Every green herb and herbs bearing seed have been given by God to be used for food.

A newly planted tree producing edible food shall not be eaten for the first three years it produces. In the fourth year all its fruit shall be an offering to God. In the fifth year the fruit of the tree may be eaten.
Every tree which bears fruit yielding seed was made by God to be eaten as food.
You are not to sow your vineyards with divers seeds: least all the produce of the seed which you have sown, and the fruit of the vineyard become defiled (hybridized).
You shall not sow your field with mingled (mixed) seed, for the different kinds created were to be kept separate.
Green plants given by God for food.
You shall not eat anything which dies of itself.
That which dies of itself may be given or sold to foreigners.
One who eats any animal that died of itself shall wash his clothes and bathe, and will be unclean until evening; otherwise he will bear his iniquity.
You shall eat no manner of fat from any animal.
You shall not eat any abominable thing.
You shall not eat any manner of blood from fowl or beast either by itself or with its flesh.
You are not to boil a kid in the milk of its mother.
Abstain from animals that were strangled.
Admonished not to drink strong drink and become drunk.
You shall not eat any flesh that is torn of beasts in the field, you shall cast it to the dogs.
Admonishment against gluttony and overeating.
Fast observed on occasions of judgments of God.
Fasting is not to be made a subject of display.
Fasting is to be unto God.
Fasting for private afflictions.
You shall 'afflict your souls' (fast) on the Day of Atonement.
Fasting accompanied by confession of sin.
Public fasts proclaimed.
Fasting accompanied by prayer.
You are not to disfigure your body by making any cuttings in your flesh or tattoo marks in your skin.
God promises health and to heal sickness of those who will pray to Him for it.
We are to praise God for recovery from sickness.
You shall touch no unclean thing, nor touch the carcass of any unclean beast.
Cleansing of a woman after child birth.
Laws concerning women during menstruation.
Pregnant women are not to take alcoholic drink.
Laws concerning bodily discharges and cleansing.
All male children born are to be circumcised on the eighth day after birth.
Those with a plague or contagious diseases are to be quarantined.
He that touches the dead body of any man shall be unclean seven days.
Lepers are to be cleansed.
A house occupied by one having a plague or contagious disease is to be cleaned and disinfected.
For him that is sick, let him call for the elders of the church, and let them pray over him.
Laws of purification.
The prayer of faith will save the sick, and the Lord will raise him up.
Laws concerning contact with dead or unclean things.
Garments worn by one who has a contagious disease are to be burned.
All things that touch a dead unclean animal must be cleansed with water and allowed to set until evening.
Those who are sick or have a contagious disease shall not conceal their condition but are to alert others as to their condition.
Health and healing come from obedience to the word and law of God.
God puts disease and sickness on those who will not heed his commandments and keep his statutes.
We are to be charitable to the poor and hungry.
Acts of uncharitableness towards the poor are condemned.
If because of food your brother is hurt, you are no longer walking charitably.
The love of God does not dwell in those that are uncharitable.
It is more blessed to give than to receive.
Every man is to give according to the purpose that God has placed in his heart.
Do not neglect to show hospitality to strangers, for by so doing some have entertained angels without knowing it.
Charity and love is to be sought above all things.
We are to be hospitable towards one another without grudging.
Give not grudgingly or of necessity, for God loves a cheerful giver.
Aid and hospitality is to be given to the poor.
The righteous man gives his bread to the hungry, and covers the naked with clothing, but the unrighteous man who oppresses the poor and needy shall not live.
Charity shall cover a multitude of sins.
Let no one seek his own good, but that of his neighbor.
Uncharitableness brings a curse.
Give to him who asks of you, and do not turn away from him who wants to borrow from you.
A care for the poor is a characteristic of the righteous.
We should defend the poor and deliver them from the hand of the wicked.
If one of your brethren becomes poor and falls into poverty among you, you are to sustain him, whether he be a foreigner or a countryman.
Do not harden your heart towards the poor but lend to him sufficient to cover his need.
You are not to mock the poor.
You shall not oppress the poor.
He who oppresses the poor reproaches his Maker, but he who honors his Maker has mercy towards the needy.
Neglect towards to poor and hungry is a neglect of Christ.
The poor you will always have with you.
He who neglects the needy does not have the love of God in him.
Curses and punishments are due to those who neglect the poor or withhold from him his needs.
God will bless and deliver him that gives consideration to the poor.
He that is gracious to a poor man lends to God, and He will repay him for his good deed.
We should give of that which we have extra to the poor.
The poor will never cease out of the land, therefore open your hand wide to your poor brethren.
We should be of aid and help to the fatherless and widows with their afflictions.
Do not take a widow's raiment in pledge.
You shall not afflict or oppress any widow or fatherless child.
We should defend the fatherless and needy and plead for the widow.
Curses and Punishments will befall those who neglect or cause affliction to the fatherless and widows.
We should visit orphans and widows in their trouble.
Honor widows who are really widows (those 60 years old and up and been the wife of one man).
We are not to curse the deaf or put a stumbling block before the blind.
Cursed be he that causes the blind to wander out of the way.
We are to invite the maimed, the lame and the blind to our feasts.
Show respect for the aged.
You should support and help the weak.
A small portion of crops are to remain unharvested or unpicked so that they may be left for the poor and fatherless to take.
At the end of three years all of the tithes of the people's increase for the year are to be gathered together and given to and eaten by the stranger, the fatherless and the widow.
That of which you have extra is to be shared with the needy.
The hungry, when they come to a neighbor's vineyard, may eat their fill of grapes, but shall not put any in their basket.
Give to every man that asks and needs, for whatever measure you deal out to others, it will be dealt to you in return.
The needy may enter their neighbor's grain fields and corn fields and pluck the crop by hand, but shall not cut down the crop with a sickle.
Individual offerings, donations, and contributions are to be given according to the purpose that one's heart leads, giving to the poor willingly.
Poverty is derived from laziness and a lack of work effort.
He who loves pleasure will become a poor man.
Poverty will come to him who refuses instruction and is unwilling to learn.
He who follows empty pursuits will have poverty in plenty.
Idle chatter leads only to poverty.
Poverty will come to the drunkard and the glutton.
He who oppresses the poor to increase his riches will surely come to poverty.
Poverty caused by love of sleep.
God will not allow the soul of the righteous to famish, but He casts away the substance of the wicked.
He becomes poor that deals with a slack hand, but into the hand of the diligent comes wealth.
There shall be a cancellation of debt every seven years - a creditor can only hold a debt for 6 years and must release the obligation on the seventh year.
Debts of foreigners may be continued beyond seven years.
Those who need to borrow from you are not to be turned away.
The borrower is servant to the lender.

You shall not think evil and withhold loaning to your brother in need because the Seventh Year, the year of release, is at hand. You shall surely give to him and the LORD will bless you in all your works.
It is wicked to borrow and not repay.
Lend to the poor and needy what is sufficient for his needs.
It is best to owe no man any thing.
Items necessary to sustain a livelihood are not to be given as a pledge (security) for a debt.
You shall not take a widow's garment as a pledge.
Warnings against giving sureties for debts of others.
He who is surety for a stranger will suffer for it, but one who hates being surety is secure.
Pledges given by the poor for debt are not to be retained overnight.
When you lend your brother anything you shall not go into his house to take his pledge, but rather he shall bring the pledge out to you.
The righteous man restores to the debtor his pledge, but the unrighteous does not restore a pledge.
Produce, commodities, and money are to follow just weights and measures in their use and exchange.
A just weight and balance are of God's work.
Those who use unjust and deceitful weights are wicked.
You shall not have in your bag differing weights, a heavy and light. You shall not have in your house differing measures, large and a small. You shall have a perfect and just weight and measure.
A false balance and diverse weights and measures are an abomination to the LORD; but a just weight is His delight.
Punishments for not using just weights and measures.
If you lend to any of your brethren in need, you are not to take or lay usury upon them.
No substance loaned or borrowed is to be repaid with increase or interest-no usury of money, or food, or of anything that is borrowed.
You may charge usury to a foreigner.
Usury and the usurer are condemned.
If one of your brethren becomes poor, you shall exact no usury or interest from him; you shall not lend him your money for usury, nor lend him your food at a profit.
Usury is regarded as dishonest profit.
Usury is an iniquity, for the righteous man does not lend money on interest or take increase.
He who does not put out his money at usury may dwell in the LORD's holy nation.
Sons are not to suffer punishment for usury exacted by their fathers.
You are not to deal dishonestly or falsely with others when you buy and sell.
When you sell to your neighbor or buy from your neighbor, you shall not oppress one another.
You shall not be unrighteous or have unjust gain in trading, selling or buying.
Free enterprise is recognized in trading and selling of all kinds of wares.
Better is a little with righteousness, than vast revenues without justice.
Ill-gotten gains do not profit.
Sale of goods.
Taxes are paid for the support of godly governments.
A poll or head tax can be levied (which is to be of a small amount) according to a census taken on persons of a certain age.
All men subject to a poll tax are to pay the same amount (the rich shall not pay more, and the poor less).
Every man shall give as he is able, according to the blessings God has given him (advalorern tax).
Abusive and heavy taxation leads to rebellion by the people.
Abusive and heavy taxation causes an impoverished nation and burdensome debts.
Oppressive taxation is often due to the sins of the nation.
Tithes and offerings collected as taxes are to be put into the treasury.
It is unlawful to impose a toll, tribute, or custom tax upon any priest or ministerial aide.
A tarriff or excise tax levied on the traffic of imported merchandise.
Money is to be of a standard fixed weight of a precious metal (silver, gold, etc.).
Money (silver) is used in the sale and purchase of land and commodities.
